domains.name: Conceptual Literacy
domains.description: Measures whether the learner understands the language, structure, and foundational concepts of AI. Covers the ability to speak clearly about AI ideas and distinguish related terms accurately.

domains.name: LLM Mechanics
domains.description: Measures whether the learner understands how modern language models behave in practice, including their constraints, reliability characteristics, and cost and latency tradeoffs.

domains.name: AI-Assisted Development Workflow
domains.description: Measures how effectively the learner uses AI tools in day-to-day software development, from autocomplete through full coding agents, and how safely they verify AI output.

domains.name: AI System Design
domains.description: Measures the learner's ability to design and build systems that use AI rather than merely consuming AI outputs, including retrieval, tool use, orchestration, and evaluation.

domains.name: Operational Readiness
domains.description: Measures the surrounding engineering maturity needed to work effectively with AI systems, spanning the shell, version control, environments, containers, secrets, deployment, and observability.

subdomains.name: AI, ML, DL, NLP, and LLM distinctions
subdomains.description: The nested relationships among artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, and large language models.

subdomains.name: Training versus inference
subdomains.description: What differs between the training phase, where a model learns from data, and the inference phase, where a deployed model produces outputs.

subdomains.name: Neural networks and transformers
subdomains.description: The conceptual role of neural networks and the transformer architecture that underpins modern language models.

subdomains.name: Tokens and embeddings (conceptual)
subdomains.description: A conceptual understanding of how text is broken into tokens and represented as embeddings, without requiring implementation detail.

subdomains.name: Vector concepts and retrieval basics
subdomains.description: The conceptual basis of vector representations, similarity, and how they enable retrieval of relevant information.

subdomains.name: Relationships between major AI terms
subdomains.description: How the major AI terms fit together into a coherent mental model rather than a list of isolated buzzwords.

subdomains.name: Tokens and token limits
subdomains.description: How tokenization works in practice and how token limits constrain inputs, outputs, and cost.

subdomains.name: Context windows
subdomains.description: How the finite context window governs what a model can attend to and how content is truncated or dropped.

subdomains.name: Prompt structure
subdomains.description: How the arrangement of instructions, context, and examples in a prompt shapes model behavior and output quality.

subdomains.name: Memory limitations
subdomains.description: Why models do not inherently remember prior turns beyond the supplied context and how apparent memory is engineered.

subdomains.name: Model size tradeoffs
subdomains.description: How model size relates to capability, speed, and cost, and when a smaller model is the better choice.

subdomains.name: Latency and cost
subdomains.description: The practical latency and cost drivers of LLM usage and the levers available to manage them.

subdomains.name: Temperature and output control
subdomains.description: How sampling parameters such as temperature influence determinism, creativity, and reliability of outputs.

subdomains.name: Hallucinations and reliability
subdomains.description: Why models produce confident but incorrect output and how reliability can be assessed and improved.

subdomains.name: Autocomplete
subdomains.description: Using inline AI autocomplete suggestions effectively while retaining control over correctness.

subdomains.name: Code generation
subdomains.description: Prompting AI tools to generate larger blocks of code and integrating that code responsibly.

subdomains.name: Debugging with AI
subdomains.description: Using AI assistance to localize, explain, and resolve defects.

subdomains.name: Test generation
subdomains.description: Using AI to generate and strengthen automated tests while ensuring they are meaningful.

subdomains.name: Refactoring support
subdomains.description: Using AI to restructure existing code safely without changing its behavior.

subdomains.name: AI-assisted documentation
subdomains.description: Using AI to draft and maintain documentation that stays accurate and useful.

subdomains.name: Review and verification workflows
subdomains.description: Establishing habits that verify AI-generated changes before they are trusted or merged.

subdomains.name: AI coding agents
subdomains.description: Directing autonomous or semi-autonomous coding agents that can plan and execute multi-step tasks.

subdomains.name: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
subdomains.description: Grounding model responses in retrieved external content and knowing when this pattern applies.

subdomains.name: Embeddings and chunking
subdomains.description: Producing embeddings and splitting source content into chunks suitable for retrieval.

subdomains.name: Vector search
subdomains.description: Storing and querying embeddings to find semantically relevant content.

subdomains.name: Tool calling
subdomains.description: Enabling a model to invoke external functions or tools and use their results.

subdomains.name: Structured output
subdomains.description: Constraining model output to reliable, machine-parseable structures such as JSON schemas.

subdomains.name: Memory patterns
subdomains.description: Engineering persistence of relevant state across turns or sessions in an AI application.

subdomains.name: Orchestration and agent loops
subdomains.description: Coordinating multi-step reasoning, tool use, and control flow in agentic systems.

subdomains.name: Evaluation patterns
subdomains.description: Measuring the quality, correctness, and regressions of AI system behavior.

subdomains.name: Human-in-the-loop design
subdomains.description: Designing checkpoints where humans review, approve, or correct AI actions.

subdomains.name: Shell fluency
subdomains.description: Comfortably composing shell commands, pipes, and scripts to accomplish engineering tasks.

subdomains.name: Terminal usage
subdomains.description: Working productively in a terminal environment, including navigation and process control.

subdomains.name: tmux and terminal multiplexing
subdomains.description: Using terminal multiplexers to manage multiple sessions and long-running work.

subdomains.name: Git and worktrees
subdomains.description: Using version control effectively, including branching and worktree-based isolation.

subdomains.name: Package and environment management
subdomains.description: Managing dependencies and reproducible environments across projects and machines.

subdomains.name: Containers
subdomains.description: Using containers to package and isolate applications and their dependencies.

subdomains.name: Secrets handling
subdomains.description: Managing API keys and credentials securely rather than exposing them in code or logs.

subdomains.name: Deployment basics
subdomains.description: Getting an application running in a hosted environment and understanding release fundamentals.

subdomains.name: Monitoring and logs
subdomains.description: Observing running systems through logs and metrics to detect and diagnose problems.

subdomains.name: Local versus hosted model workflows
subdomains.description: Choosing between running models locally and using hosted APIs based on the tradeoffs involved.

competencies.statement: The learner can distinguish AI, machine learning, deep learning, NLP, and LLMs and describe how they relate.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by correctly placing each term in its nested relationship and selecting accurate definitions over conflated ones.

competencies.statement: The learner can classify a given example system or technique under the correct AI category.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by mapping concrete examples, such as a spam filter or a chatbot, to the appropriate field like ML or NLP without over-generalizing to AI.

competencies.statement: The learner can explain the difference between training and inference and identify which phase a described activity belongs to.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by distinguishing model-development activities from deployment-time activities and recognizing that inference does not update the model's weights.

competencies.statement: The learner can describe at a conceptual level what neural networks and transformers do and why transformers enabled modern LLMs.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by explaining ideas such as learned parameters and attention in plain language without requiring mathematical detail.

competencies.statement: The learner can explain conceptually what tokens and embeddings are and how they differ.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by describing tokens as units of text and embeddings as numeric meaning representations, and identifying which is relevant to a scenario.

competencies.statement: The learner can explain how vector similarity enables retrieval of relevant information.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by describing why semantically similar items sit close together in vector space and how that supports search.

competencies.statement: The learner can distinguish semantic (vector) retrieval from exact keyword lookup at a conceptual level.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by identifying when meaning-based matching is preferable to literal string matching and vice versa.

competencies.statement: The learner can assemble the major AI terms into a coherent mental model and identify inaccurate relationships between them.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by selecting statements that correctly relate terms and rejecting ones that misstate how the concepts connect.

competencies.statement: The learner can explain what tokens are and how token limits constrain prompts and responses.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by relating text length to token counts and predicting when input or output will exceed a limit.

competencies.statement: The learner can estimate the cost and feasibility implications of token usage for a given task.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by reasoning about how larger inputs or outputs increase cost and choosing token-efficient approaches.

competencies.statement: The learner can explain what a context window is and how it bounds what the model can consider.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by describing the window as the total tokens available for input plus output and its practical limits.

competencies.statement: The learner can diagnose degraded behavior in long conversations as a context-window limitation.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by attributing dropped or inconsistent earlier content to truncation or window overflow rather than unrelated causes.

competencies.statement: The learner can structure a prompt with clear instructions, context, and examples to improve output quality.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by selecting or composing prompts whose organization reliably produces the intended result.

competencies.statement: The learner can explain why a stateless model does not inherently remember prior interactions and how apparent memory is provided.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by recognizing that history must be re-supplied in context and distinguishing true persistence from re-sent context.

competencies.statement: The learner can reason about tradeoffs between larger and smaller models for capability, speed, and cost.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by choosing an appropriately sized model for a scenario and justifying the tradeoff.

competencies.statement: The learner can identify the primary drivers of LLM latency and cost in an application.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by attributing slowness or expense to factors such as model choice, token volume, or call frequency.

competencies.statement: The learner can select practical levers to reduce cost or latency without unacceptable quality loss.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by choosing tactics such as smaller models, caching, shorter context, or batching appropriate to a scenario.

competencies.statement: The learner can explain how temperature and related sampling controls affect output determinism and variability.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by predicting how raising or lowering temperature changes results and choosing a setting fit for a task.

competencies.statement: The learner can explain why LLMs hallucinate and recognize outputs that require verification.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by identifying confident but unfounded output and describing the conditions that make hallucination more likely.

competencies.statement: The learner can select strategies to improve reliability and reduce hallucination risk.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by choosing mitigations such as grounding, retrieval, citations, or verification steps appropriate to a scenario.

competencies.statement: The learner can use inline autocomplete suggestions productively while judging when to accept, edit, or reject them.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by selecting workflows that leverage suggestions without blindly accepting incorrect completions.

competencies.statement: The learner can prompt an AI tool to generate a code block that meets stated requirements.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by framing requirements and constraints so generated code is usable with minimal rework.

competencies.statement: The learner can integrate and adapt AI-generated code safely into an existing codebase.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by reconciling generated code with existing conventions, interfaces, and constraints rather than pasting it verbatim.

competencies.statement: The learner can use AI assistance to localize and explain a defect from an error or symptom.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by supplying the right context to an AI tool and interpreting its explanation to narrow down a bug.

competencies.statement: The learner can validate an AI-proposed fix before applying it.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by reasoning about whether a suggested fix addresses the root cause and confirming it through tests or inspection.

competencies.statement: The learner can use AI to generate tests and judge whether those tests are meaningful.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by directing test generation toward important behavior and rejecting trivial or tautological tests.

competencies.statement: The learner can use AI to refactor code while preserving behavior.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by scoping refactors, relying on tests, and confirming that behavior is unchanged after AI-assisted restructuring.

competencies.statement: The learner can use AI to draft documentation and verify its accuracy against the code.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by generating docs and correcting statements that do not match actual behavior or interfaces.

competencies.statement: The learner can apply a review and verification workflow before trusting AI-generated changes.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by selecting steps such as reading the diff, running tests, and checking edge cases before accepting or merging.

competencies.statement: The learner can identify what to verify first when AI output looks plausible but may be wrong.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by prioritizing checks on correctness-critical assumptions rather than superficial style when reviewing AI output.

competencies.statement: The learner can direct an AI coding agent to complete a multi-step task with appropriate scoping and guardrails.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by giving an agent a clear goal, constraints, and checkpoints rather than an open-ended instruction.

competencies.statement: The learner can evaluate when using an autonomous coding agent is appropriate versus a more manual approach.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by weighing task risk, verifiability, and cost to decide how much autonomy to grant.

competencies.statement: The learner can explain how retrieval-augmented generation grounds responses in external content.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by describing the retrieve-then-generate flow and how retrieved context reduces reliance on parametric knowledge.

competencies.statement: The learner can decide when RAG is the appropriate approach versus fine-tuning or a plain prompt.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by matching RAG to problems involving changing or proprietary knowledge and choosing alternatives when better suited.

competencies.statement: The learner can explain the role of embeddings and chunking in a retrieval pipeline.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by describing how source content is split and embedded so it can later be retrieved by similarity.

competencies.statement: The learner can choose a chunking strategy appropriate to the content and retrieval goal.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by reasoning about chunk size and overlap tradeoffs and their effect on retrieval quality.

competencies.statement: The learner can describe how a vector store indexes and returns the most relevant results for a query.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by explaining nearest-neighbor retrieval over embeddings and the role of top-k selection.

competencies.statement: The learner can explain what problem tool calling solves and how a model invokes an external tool.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by describing how a model requests a function with arguments and incorporates the returned result.

competencies.statement: The learner can design a tool interface a model can call reliably.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by defining clear tool names, parameters, and descriptions that reduce misuse and ambiguity.

competencies.statement: The learner can constrain model output to a structured, machine-parseable format and handle failures.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by specifying a schema, validating output, and planning for cases where the model deviates from it.

competencies.statement: The learner can select a memory pattern to persist relevant state across turns or sessions.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by choosing between approaches such as summarization, storage, and retrieval to maintain continuity.

competencies.statement: The learner can describe how an agent loop coordinates reasoning, tool calls, and control flow.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by explaining the observe-decide-act cycle and how a loop terminates or escalates.

competencies.statement: The learner can identify failure modes in agent orchestration and select mitigations.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by recognizing risks such as infinite loops, runaway cost, or compounding errors and choosing safeguards.

competencies.statement: The learner can choose an evaluation approach to measure the quality of an AI system's output.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by selecting suitable evaluation methods such as reference comparison, rubric scoring, or human review for a scenario.

competencies.statement: The learner can design an evaluation that detects regressions as an AI system changes.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by defining representative test cases and metrics that catch quality drops when prompts or models change.

competencies.statement: The learner can design human-in-the-loop checkpoints for high-risk AI actions.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by placing review or approval steps where the cost of an unchecked error is highest.

competencies.statement: The learner can compose shell commands, pipes, and redirection to accomplish common tasks.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by chaining commands to filter, transform, and move data without resorting to manual steps.

competencies.statement: The learner can write a simple shell script to automate a repetitive workflow.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by combining commands, variables, and control flow into a reusable script.

competencies.statement: The learner can navigate the filesystem and manage processes productively in a terminal.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by moving between directories, inspecting files, and starting, backgrounding, or stopping processes.

competencies.statement: The learner can use a terminal multiplexer to manage multiple sessions and long-running work.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by creating and switching between panes or windows and keeping processes alive across disconnects.

competencies.statement: The learner can use git branching and commits to isolate and review changes safely.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by structuring work into branches and commits that keep changes reviewable and reversible.

competencies.statement: The learner can explain how git worktrees support parallel work, including parallel AI-assisted development.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by describing how worktrees provide isolated checkouts so multiple efforts proceed without interfering.

competencies.statement: The learner can manage dependencies and reproducible environments across machines.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by using lockfiles or environment definitions so a project installs consistently for others.

competencies.statement: The learner can explain how containers package and isolate an application with its dependencies.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by describing the difference between an image and a running container and why isolation aids reproducibility.

competencies.statement: The learner can decide when containerizing a workload is worthwhile.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by weighing portability and consistency benefits against added complexity for a given scenario.

competencies.statement: The learner can handle secrets such as API keys securely rather than exposing them.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by using environment variables or secret stores and keeping credentials out of source control and logs.

competencies.statement: The learner can deploy an application to a hosted environment and describe the basic release steps.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by getting an app running remotely and explaining build, configuration, and rollout fundamentals.

competencies.statement: The learner can identify configuration and environment differences that affect a deployed application.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by recognizing how environment variables, dependencies, and resources differ between local and hosted runs.

competencies.statement: The learner can use logs and basic metrics to detect and diagnose problems in a running system.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by locating relevant log output and interpreting signals to identify the source of an issue.

competencies.statement: The learner can explain the tradeoffs between running models locally and using hosted model APIs.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by comparing factors such as cost, latency, privacy, and control when choosing an approach.

competencies.statement: The learner can select a local or hosted model workflow appropriate to a given constraint.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by matching a workflow to requirements such as data privacy, offline use, or scale.
